paths.description: Homepage: top-level discovery, navigation, consent, performance, security, and mobile adaptation.
World section listing: representative category/index template.
Current news article: representative core reading journey and article metadata/no-JS behavior.
Invalid route: recovery and HTTP failure-state behavior.

findings.summary: The site does not provide a user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under default and prefers-color-scheme: dark retain the same white content surface and consent UI; the platform probe found no theme adaptation signal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens across page and consent surfaces.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe matched reduce but found no reduced-motion stylesheet rule and still found 11 animations, including a running 300 ms animation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that removes non-essential motion and stops auto-advance.

findings.summary: Page and route changes do not use View Transitions.
findings.evidence: The live CSS probe found no view-transition rules on this multi-page news site.
findings.suggestedFix: Use cross-document View Transitions for compatible article and section navigation, with a non-animated fallback.

findings.summary: The long news page has no declarative scroll-driven interaction treatment.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no animation-timeline or scroll-timeline on a 25,433 px home page.
findings.suggestedFix: Where scroll-linked effects are useful, implement them with CSS scroll-driven animations rather than script listeners.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial obscures all news content on every tested entry page.
findings.evidence: Desktop, mobile, article, listing, and media screenshots all open with a large modal covering the primary content; on mobile it occupies nearly the full viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, non-blocking consent surface where legally possible and provide an immediate, equally prominent reject option.

findings.summary: The blocking consent UI is not exposed as a native dialog.
findings.evidence: The DOM/platform probe found zero dialog, popover, or details elements while screenshots show a modal interstitial.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the modal with <dialog>, correct labelling, focus trapping/restoration, Escape handling, and a clear dismiss/reject action.

findings.summary: Components rely on page-level responsive CSS rather than container queries.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no @container rules across a dense reusable card layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt container queries for reusable news cards and navigation components that appear in differently sized regions.

findings.summary: Many controls are too small and keyboard focus is not visibly styled.
findings.evidence: Of 786 visible controls, 297 measured below 24 px in at least one dimension; the first 20 focused links all computed outline-style none and no focus box shadow.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide clearly visible :focus-visible styles and increase interactive target areas toward 44 CSS px without changing visual density unnecessarily.

findings.summary: The homepage is very slow and unstable in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 8.3 s, CLS 1.037, TBT 840 ms, Speed Index 22.3 s, and performance score 0.18.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP resource, reserve all late content space, reduce blocking JavaScript, and gate advertising work until after critical content.

findings.summary: The homepage transfers an excessive resource payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 274 requests and 8,827,956 transferred bytes, including 4.98 MB of images and 3.03 MB of scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a page-weight budget, optimize LCP discovery, defer non-critical ads/widgets, and deliver responsive modern images.

findings.summary: Third-party and device-detection JavaScript dominates delivery.
findings.evidence: HAR shows 56 scripts / 3.03 MB; a single uncompressed device_model_min.js is 628,959 bytes and Google Tag Manager resources add hundreds of KB.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate analytics, conditionally load device/ad code, compress remaining scripts, and audit code coverage.

findings.summary: Interactive controls and images have accessibility naming failures.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name and link-name; the image audit found 3 missing alt values and the form probe found unlabelled fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Use semantic controls and provide accessible names, associated labels, and meaningful alt text.

findings.summary: Foreground/background combinations fail minimum contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse color-contrast audit scored 0 and lists failing elements.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust text and control color tokens to meet WCAG AA in every state, including the consent surface.

findings.summary: Heading and landmark structure is noisy and focus visibility is absent.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order; the platform probe found no main landmark, multiple H1s from consent UI, and focused links with outline none.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one main landmark, preserve logical heading order, keep the consent title out of the document content hierarchy, and add :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The page logs browser errors.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse errors-in-console audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Resolve each production console error and add monitoring/regression checks for uncaught exceptions.

findings.summary: The page uses deprecated APIs and prompts for notifications on load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported one deprecated API, inspector issues, and a notification permission request at startup.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove deprecated calls and request notification permission only after an explicit, contextual user action.

findings.summary: Hundreds of interactions use non-crawlable javascript: links.
findings.evidence: The live probe found 332 javascript: anchors and Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href URLs for navigation and buttons for actions, with descriptive accessible text.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP policy leave avoidable security gaps.
findings.evidence: Cookies audit found 23 of 24 cookies without Secure; many use SameSite=None. CSP allows unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, choose Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is required, and migrate toward nonce/hash-based CSP without unsafe-eval.

findings.summary: The page has a very large advertising and tracking footprint.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 49 third-party origins and 14 known tracker domains; HAR attributed 262 requests and 8.58 MB to non-main origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimize vendors, load optional analytics only after valid consent, batch essential events, and enforce a third-party byte/request budget.

findings.summary: Notification permission is requested without user context.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse notification-on-start audit scored 0.
findings.suggestedFix: Ask for notification permission only after the user chooses a clear subscribe/alerts action.

findings.summary: Permissions-Policy is missing and CSP defenses are weakened.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence shows no Permissions-Policy and a CSP containing unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a least-privilege Permissions-Policy and strengthen CSP while preserving HSTS, nosniff, frame, and referrer protections.

findings.summary: An invalid URL produces a bare 406 response with no recovery path.
findings.evidence: The tested nonexistent route rendered only “406 Not Acceptable”, with an empty title and no links.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a proper 404 page with site navigation, search, a home link, and a concise recovery message.

findings.summary: Only a minority of rendered words are present to a non-JavaScript crawler.
findings.evidence: Discoverability measured 24% raw/rendered word coverage on home and 31% on an article, although both were non-shell HTML with core metadata.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the complete primary article/list content and reserve JavaScript for enhancement.

findings.summary: The first consent layer lacks an equally prominent reject action.
findings.evidence: Screenshots offer Consent and Manage options but no direct Reject all action, while listing 319 partners and blocking content.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer Reject all beside Accept all with equal visual weight, concise purposes, and easy later withdrawal.

findings.summary: Search inputs are unlabelled and disable autocomplete.
findings.evidence: The form probe found text inputs without labels; the q search field sets autocomplete=off.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit labels or accessible names and retain helpful browser input assistance unless there is a documented reason not to.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not resource-efficient.
findings.evidence: Of 100 inspected images, 99 lacked dimensions, 67 lacked srcset, 87 used legacy formats, and 17 were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic dimensions, responsive srcset/sizes, and AVIF/WebP variants; right-size decorative assets.

findings.summary: Third-party resource use is disproportionate for reading news.
findings.evidence: The homepage transferred 8.83 MB; 8.58 MB and 262 requests were classified off the main origin, including a broad ad-tech stack.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce vendor, request, and byte budgets; defer non-essential media and third parties until interaction/consent.

findings.summary: The initial page has a very large heap and DOM-related footprint.
findings.evidence: Baseline heap summary contained 1,003,009 nodes and 60.9 MB self size for the news homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce shipped widgets, hidden DOM, ad-tech allocations, and retained component state; monitor heap/node budgets.

findings.summary: Reading the news is blocked before the first article interaction.
findings.evidence: Every tested page archetype opened behind the consent interstitial, forcing a detour before the primary reading task.
findings.suggestedFix: Let users continue with an explicit reject choice from the first layer and keep the reading path visible.

findings.summary: The error state offers no recovery.
findings.evidence: The invalid route displays only 406 Not Acceptable, without search, back, home, or retry actions.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide branded 404/5xx states with clear status and recovery controls.

taskList.title: Cut LCP/CLS, JavaScript, image, and third-party payloads
Replace the blocking consent experience with equal accept/reject choices and semantic dialog behavior
Reduce tracking and harden cookies, CSP, and browser policies
Repair accessible names, contrast, headings, landmarks, focus, and target sizes
Provide complete server-rendered content, crawlable links, and useful failure pages
Add preference-aware theming and reduced-motion behavior
